title: SAXON Q Introduces Patented Quantum Watchdog System for Runtime QPU Fault Detection - Quantum Computing Report
author: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
text:
Leipzig-based nitrogen-vacancy (NV) diamond quantum computing company SAXON Q has announced Quantum Watchdog, a hardware-agnostic safety and diagnostic architecture engineered to detect physical hardware failures in quantum processors during live operation and transition compromised units into a safe state. Designed to complement quantum error correction by catching hardware degradation, environmental drift, or tampering rather than stochastic qubit noise, the system targets edge deployments in defense, robotics, and automotive environments as well as multi-QPU high-performance computing (HPC) clusters.

Operating on an independent classical processor equipped with isolated clocks, timers, and environmental sensors, Quantum Watchdog monitors physical telemetry, including power draw, temperature, and ambient magnetic fields, while periodically interleaving verified test calculations into active user workloads. Depending on operational criticality, users can allocate up to 50% of processor runtime to diagnostic verification or restrict checks to startup and intermittent intervals. For multi-core configurations, the architecture implements dual-processor comparison or majority-voting redundancy across three or more processors to isolate and shut down malfunctioning units without halting cluster execution.

While compatible across superconducting, trapped-ion, and quantum sensing modalities, the system will first be offered as a configurable option on SAXON Q’s room-temperature SXQ128 and SXQ512 multi-core processors by dedicating an onboard control circuit to safety monitoring. Protected by granted patents in Europe, the United States, and China, Quantum Watchdog is slated for initial custom implementation in early 2027 alongside OEM and system integrator licensing, with formally safety-certified versions scheduled to follow after independent auditing and field testing.
